text: During a normal day, a consumer or professional might encounter a massive local trend long before Wall Street analysts notice it. Investing in what you know gives you an incredible informational edge.
source: Peter Lynch — One Up On Wall Street
author: Peter Lynch

text: A 'ten-bagger' is a stock that returns ten times your initial investment. You only need a few of these in a lifetime to make serious money, but they require the patience to hold onto great companies through market fluctuations.
source: Peter Lynch — One Up On Wall Street
author: Peter Lynch

text: The P/E ratio of any company that's fairly priced will equal its growth rate. If a company is growing at 15 percent a year and trading at a P/E of 15, it's fairly priced; if it trades at a P/E of 10, it's a bargain.
source: Peter Lynch — One Up On Wall Street
author: Peter Lynch

text: When companies acquire businesses they know nothing about in the name of diversification, it almost always leads to a drop in earnings and stock price. This is what I call 'diworsification'.
source: Peter Lynch — One Up On Wall Street
author: Peter Lynch
